chunks: 1231 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“There is no harm in a man speaking when the Imam has finished the sermon on Friday, in the interval between that and the establishment of the salat (prayer). Whether he hears the recitation or does not hear it, it suffices him.”

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it was sufficient for him; it fulfilled the required minimum
key_terms.الْخُطْبَةِ: the Friday sermon delivered before the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.تُقَامَ الصَّلَاةُ: the salat (prayer) is formally commenced or established
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, specifically in the context of Jumuʿah worship

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak after the Friday sermon before the salat (prayer) begins?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about conduct on Friday after the Imam completes the sermon and before the salat (prayer) begins. It indicates that speaking during this interval is permissible, and that hearing or not hearing the recitation does not invalidate sufficiency in this context.
